finding.title: Log the malformed-days_of_week fallback in StageDefinitionCodec.decode instead of silently defaulting to []
finding.why: This legacy-quartet fallback (pre-`schedule`-column documents) swallows any jsonDecode/cast failure on days_of_week and silently substitutes an empty day list, changing a family's stage-due schedule with no AppLogger trail. Nobody could diagnose why a days_of_week schedule stopped firing for a given track.
finding.recommendation: Log via AppLogger (including the raw malformed value, at debug/warn level) before falling back to const [].
acceptance_criteria: Test feeds a malformed days_of_week string into decode() and asserts an AppLogger call occurs alongside the [] fallback.

finding.title: Update BookmarkCodec's dual-key comment — it describes the pre-Phase-B bug as still live

evidence.quote: // Dual-key: live writers (BookmarkEntity.toFirestore et al.) persist the ref
/// Phase B: routes through [BookmarkCodec.encode] so the write shape is

finding.why: bookmark.dart's own comment confirms Phase B already made BookmarkEntity.toFirestore route through this exact codec, which writes sefaria_ref, not content_item_id. bookmark_codec.dart's comment still describes 'live writers... persist the ref under content_item_id' in the present tense, as if that writer still exists today. A future maintainer reading only this file would wrongly conclude content_item_id is still being actively written and might be reluctant to ever retire the read-side fallback, or misdiagnose which key is canonical.
finding.recommendation: Reword to past tense: 'Pre-Phase-B documents may still carry content_item_id; decode() accepts both for backward-compatible reads.'
acceptance_criteria: Comment reworded to past tense; no behavior change.

finding.title: Add `_codec.dart` to coding-standards.md's File Naming Conventions table — 15 files use it, no documented suffix fits

evidence.quote: All Dart files use **snake_case**. The file suffix encodes its architectural role:
/// Abstract base for per-entity Firestore ↔ Dart codecs.

finding.why: The suffix table (coding-standards.md lines 560-577) lists `_dto` ('Firestore / JSON boundary') and `_mapper` ('Converts between layers') as the two closest documented roles, but every file in core/sync/codec/ (15 files, ~1370 lines, entirely consistent) combines both responsibilities under `_codec` — a suffix absent from the table. The convention is clearly deliberate and repo-wide, not a one-off typo, so the table is what's stale, not the code.
finding.recommendation: Add a `_codec.dart` row to the table (role: combined Firestore wire-format encode/decode for one entity — a merged DTO+mapper) rather than proposing a 15-file rename with no behavioral benefit.
acceptance_criteria: coding-standards.md's File Naming Conventions table includes a `_codec.dart` row.

finding.title: Wire or delete dead MergeException and OutboxDeadLetterException — neither is ever thrown in lib/
finding.rule: Dead-code/lens-pass sweep (digest 'Everything' applicability) + Evans ubiquitous-language (doc must match reality); AG-6-adjacent speculative generality

evidence.quote: Callers that catch [MergeException] should record the event via crisis
thrown the item should be moved to a dead-letter queue and crisis telemetry

finding.why: Both classes' own doc comments assert they are 'Thrown when...' a specific failure occurs and that catching them triggers crisis telemetry / user-facing recovery. Exhaustive grep of lib/ for 'MergeException(' and 'OutboxDeadLetterException(' matches only their own constructor declarations — zero throw sites exist anywhere in production code (MergeException's only other reference in the whole repo is a widget test that hand-constructs it to exercise AppErrorView's generic category). The behaviors the docs promise ARE implemented — drift_merge_store.dart/profile_program_merger.dart fire merge_row_skipped and outbox_processor.dart fires outbox_dead_lettered (confirmed at outbox_processor.dart:262-272) — but entirely through inline AppLogger/analytics calls that never construct these types. A developer investigating 'why doesn't a merge failure surface a recoverable error to the user' will find MergeException, read its contract, and either burn time hunting for a throw site that doesn't exist or wrongly conclude the safety net is live when it isn't.
finding.recommendation: Either thread these into their designed throw sites (a genuinely-unrecoverable branch in drift_merge_store.dart/profile_program_merger.dart for MergeException; the max-attempts branch in outbox_processor.dart for OutboxDeadLetterException) so `is MergeException` / `is OutboxDeadLetterException` becomes meaningful to callers, or delete both classes, drop the stale W7.2 backlog line in docs/planning/tech-debt-remediation-plan.md:531, and fix the docstrings so they stop describing a control-flow path that doesn't exist.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "throw MergeException" learning_tracker/lib returns >=1 hit, or merge_exception.dart is removed and learning_screen_test.dart:80 is updated to use a type that is actually thrown in production
grep -rn "throw OutboxDeadLetterException" learning_tracker/lib returns >=1 hit, or the class is removed

finding.title: Extend FirestorePermissionDeniedException conversion beyond the 2 read call sites it currently covers
finding.rule: Nygard lens (mandatory for this area) — permission-denied at every I/O point; EH-2 typed-exception boundary

evidence.quote: Thrown when a Firestore operation returns PERMISSION_DENIED.

finding.why: _guardPermission (firestore_gateway_impl.dart:1197-1215) is the ONLY code in the app that ever throws FirestorePermissionDeniedException, and it wraps exactly 2 of this gateway's ~30 Firestore I/O methods — fetchPage (524) and fetchChildPage (1051), both reads, both with operation hardcoded to 'read'. None of the ~23 push* (write) methods route through it: pushStreak/pushSettings/pushTrack (288-337) issue raw .set() calls with no try/catch at all, and pushCompletionsBatch (246-285) wraps any commit failure — including permission-denied — as a generic SyncPushException instead. Traced end to end: OutboxProcessor absorbs every push failure internally (never rethrows to any AsyncValue/UI, so this is not a UI-facing bug), but the dedicated permission_denied analytics event in sync_orchestrator.dart (gated on `e is FirestorePermissionDeniedException`) therefore fires only from the pull path and never from an outbox push. The write path's only detector of this failure class is outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters, which pattern-matches raw persisted error text (`lastError.like('%permission-denied%')`) instead of a structured type — a duplicated, Firestore-SDK-wording-dependent re-derivation of the exact fact this exception exists to represent. This repo's own docs (on-device-preflight-cheatsheet.md, bug-hunt-findings-2026-05-31.md) call permission-denied on writes 'a known recurring failure mode in this project,' yet the typed signal for it covers roughly 1 in 15 of the gateway's I/O surface.
finding.recommendation: Route every push*/fetch* method in firestore_gateway_impl.dart through _guardPermission (or an equivalent shared wrapper) with an accurate operation value (read/write/delete) instead of only the 2 fetch methods, so FirestorePermissionDeniedException becomes the single source of truth for 'this failure was permission-denied' on both read and write paths. Then simplify outbox_dao.dart's reviveIdentityDeadLetters to check a structured signal instead of a LIKE-pattern on free text.
acceptance_criteria: count of _guardPermission( call sites in firestore_gateway_impl.dart increases beyond the current 2 to cover write (push*) methods

a new test asserts a push method (e.g. pushCompletionsBatch) surfaces FirestorePermissionDeniedException — not a generic SyncPushException/raw FirebaseException — when the underlying commit fails with code permission-denied
a test shows sync_orchestrator's permission_denied analytics event firing from a simulated outbox push failure, not only from pullOnLaunch
